facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed at Freedom Square around the clock, having set up a camp.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
The applicant spent the night of 23 to 24 February 2008 at Freedom Square.

According to the applicant, he and his companions A.Sis. and V.K. were forced into the blocking car and taken to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC).

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC) on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 a.m. by operative police officers of the PDFOC.
According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of carrying illegal arms and ammunition.
At 11.45 a.m. on 24 February 2008 the applicant was subjected to a search at the PDFOC by police officers in the presence of two attesting witnesses.
The record of the applicant's search at the PDFOC indicated that a spring baton had been found in the applicant's coat pocket.
At an unspecified hour on 24 February 2008 the applicant's car was searched at the PDFOC and a Makarov-type pistol was found.
On 24 February 2008 the applicant and the materials concerning his case were transferred from the PDFOC to Kentron Police Station of Yerevan for further inquiry.

An investigator at Kentron Police Station decided to order that the applicant undergo a forensic toxicological-chemical examination to detect use of drugs, reasoning the need for such examination by the fact that a baton had been found in the applicant's possession.
The investigator at Kentron Police Station ordered a forensic examination of the Makarov pistol found in the applicant's car.
At 11 p.m. on 24 February 2008 the applicant was taken by police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. of Kentron Police Station to the National Bureau of Examinations.
At the National Bureau of Examinations the applicant underwent the assigned forensic toxicological-chemical examination, which revealed no traces of drugs in his body.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., upon reaching Kentron Police Station the applicant had disobeyed their order to step out of the car.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant pushed police officer K.H. when leaving the car and started a scuffle with him.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant refused to enter the police building and punched police officer K.H. several times in the chest.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant was forcibly pushed into Kentron Police Station by the three officers, where he continued threatening them with violence.
On 25 February 2008 the investigator decided to institute a criminal case under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).

On 25 February 2008 at 1.35 a.m. a record of the applicant's arrest was drawn up stating that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having committed an offence under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention, finding that, if the applicant remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the investigation.
On 21 April 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan allowed the investigator's application and extended the applicant's detention by two months.

On 8 May 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the detention extension, finding that the circumstances on which the applicant's detention was based persisted, since there was still a high risk that the applicant could obstruct the investigation and abscond.
On 22 July 2008, during the first hearing, the applicant requested to be released from detention.
The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that his detention authorised by a court had expired on 15 July 2008.

The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that the judge had failed to address the issue of his detention when deciding to set the case down for trial on 14 July 2008, in violation of Articles 293 and 300 of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure.

On 22 July 2008 the judge took a decision stating that the question of the applicant's continued detention had been examined on 14 July 2008 when adopting the decision to set the case down for trial and it had been decided to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.

The judge stated on 22 July 2008 that as a result of a typographical error, the paragraph concerning the applicant's detention had not been reflected in the operative part of the decision of 14 July 2008, which was to be read as containing the phrase 'to leave the applicant's detention unchanged'.
At the next hearing on 28 July 2008 the judge presented the parties with the decision of 22 July 2008 and dismissed the applicant's request for release.

On 17 September 2008 another judge of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan who had taken over the applicant's case decided to set the case down for trial and also ruled to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.
Following the events of 1-2 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.
The events of 1-2 March 2008 in Yerevan resulted in ten deaths, including eight civilians.
The events of 1-2 March 2008 in Yerevan resulted in numerous injured persons.
Following the events of 1-2 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that a number of those officials, as well as several opposition activists, were arrested on seemingly artificial charges, which left the impression that their prosecution was politically motivated.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that according to the Helsinki Association of Armenia, a total of 14 persons were arrested and placed under investigation in the period from 20 to 29 February 2008.

Between April 2008 and June 2009 the OSCE/ODIHR (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe/Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights) conducted a monitoring project of about a hundred trials of opposition leaders and supporters related to the events of 1-2 March 2008.
